mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, discretionary trips are being displaced from shopping corridors into home-based routines, so RETAIL_REC will stay below its recent 4-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES remains below -40, TRANSIT remains below -50, and RESIDENTIAL remains above +10.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week rebound in transit access above the recent low marks a commuting normalization that quickly spills into shopping visits, lifting RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a reading below -60
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7-14 days after TRANSIT crosses up by at least 5 points from below -60, or the retail series falls further despite the transit rebound.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recover together, the combined easing of commuting constraints raises spontaneous after-work shopping more than either series alone, producing higher retail mobility over the following four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve simultaneously for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: An above-baseline PARKS surge reflects good-weather leisure substitution away from indoor retail, so retail mobility falls in the same week and the next week if park usage remains elevated.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 7 days while PARKS remains above +40, indicating park demand is not substituting for shopping trips.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in GROCERY_PHARM after the weekly peak indicate fewer essential trips and weaker overall out-of-home activity, which precede softer discretionary retail visitation over the next two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls for two consecutive weeks from a level above -10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after two straight weekly drops in GROCERY_PHARM from above -10.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT while RESIDENTIAL eases signals a genuine return to external activity, and that combination should push RETAIL_REC upward over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week average even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise and RESIDENTIAL falls for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays below -50 while TRANSIT also stays below -55, commuting restrictions or caution are still binding, and retail visits will keep underperforming on a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -50 and TRANSIT below -55
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 7 days despite WORKPLACES staying below -50 and TRANSIT staying below -55.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-spring outdoor-leisure regime, a moderate PARKS pullback from a prior spike should release demand back toward indoor retail, so RETAIL_REC improves over the next two weeks even if it stays negative.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops by at least 10 points from the prior week after exceeding +40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after PARKS falls by at least 10 points from a reading above +40.
